programme.desc: Am 08. November 1999 geht bei der Gendarmerie in Strasbourg ein ungewöhnlicher Notruf ein.

programme.title: Made in...
programme.desc: Die Zahl der tödlichen Motorradunfälle in Deutschland ist dank der verbesserten Qualität von Schutzhelmen stetig gesunken. Einen wesentlichen Anteil an dieser Entwicklung hat der Helmhersteller Schuberth.

programme.title: Made in...
programme.desc: Ein schlichtes Industriegebäude in der bayerischen Stadt Regensburg. Es ist die Heimat der innovativsten deutschen Fahrrad-Manufaktur: PG Bikes. Dort werden Elektrofahrräder im Retro-Look entwickelt und produziert .

programme.title: Kleiner AMG, großer Spaß: Der Mercedes C43 S AMG
programme.desc: Das C-Klasse Cabrio soll der Einstieg ins Cabriolet Segment von Mercedes sein. Topmodell ist das C63 Cabrio von AMG. Wem das zu teuer ist, der kann zum C43 greifen. Nur 6 statt 8 Zylinder, aber dennoch eine große Portion Sportlichkeit. Motorvision stellt den Baby AMG vor.

programme.title: Faszination Porsche mit Walter Röhrl
programme.desc: Zum 60. Jubiläum blickt Porsche auf legendäre Modelle, Motorsport-Erfolge und den Mythos 911 zurück. Walter Röhrl berichtet von Rennsiegen, technischen Innovationen und faszinierenden Sportwagen aus Zuffenhausen.

programme.title: Faszination Land Rover
programme.desc: Zum 60. Geburtstag von Land Rover stehen Defender, Discovery und Range Rover im Mittelpunkt. Die Doku zeigt legendäre Offroader, extreme Abenteuer-Touren und die Geschichte der britischen Geländewagen-Ikonen.

programme.title: Die Abschlepper
programme.desc: Abschlepper Robert Arndt räumt Münchens Straßen frei: liegengebliebene Autos, Falschparker und Unfallwagen. Die Doku zeigt stressige Einsätze, schwere Bergungen und den Alltag zwischen ADAC, Polizei und Schrottplatz.

programme.title: VW Golf VII
programme.desc: Der Golf VII - Ein Klassiker in 7. Generation

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Er hat das T im Namen. T wie Turbo. Nicht ungewöhnlich? Doch! Bei einem Ferrari schon. Der California T läutet eine neue Ära ein. Er ist nach seinem Facelift der erste Ferrari seit dem legendären bis 1992 gebauten F40, unter dessen Haube ein Turbomotor arbeitet. Selbst ein Hersteller wie Ferrari kommt also nicht am Downsizing vorbei. Ein Grund für Supercars die Turbos pfeifen zu lassen.

programme.title: Dreamcars
programme.desc: Italien ist das Land der Mode, des Designs und der aufregendsten Autos der Welt. Ferrari, Lamborghini, Maserati und Alfa Romeo gelten als Paradebeispiel für atemberaubende Autos mit tollen Formen, rassigen Motoren und unvergleichlicher Leidenschaft.

programme.title: Lamborghini vs Ferrari
programme.desc: Die Auto-Giganten der Achtziger! Kampfstier gegen Vollblut-Hengst - Ferruccio gegen Enzo... Der Lamborghini Countach Anniversary gegen den Ferrari 512 TestaRossa.

programme.title: Ferrari FF
programme.desc: Der Ferrari FF ist ein idealer Familien-Sportwagen für alle Jahreszeiten. Rennwagen und Kombi - besser hat die beiden Gegensatze noch keiner vereint. Interessant, dass dies gerade Ferrari gelingt. Und schön ist der FF auch noch - einfach eine 'Bella macchina'.

programme.title: Tradition trifft auf Moderne: Der Ferrari 488 Spider
programme.desc: Klassisches Handwerk trifft auf ein Rasiermesser-scharfes Kunstwerk. Ferrari hat seine Wurzeln auf der Rennstrecke. Der 488 bringt diese Gene auf die Straße. Motorvision ist seine 670 Pferde ausgeritten.

programme.title: Ferrari 296 GTB (2021) - Ist ein Hybrid-V6 noch ein echter Ferrari?
programme.desc: Er ist der erste V6-Mittelmotorsportwagen aus Maranello, der das Cavallino Rampante auf der Haube trägt. Der Ferrari 246 Dino von 1969 durfte das Emblem damals nicht tragen. Können seine Leistungswerte ihn vor Hohn und Spott bewahren?

programme.title: Car History
programme.desc: Ferrari. Allein der Name sorgt für einen erhöhten Puls. Bei keinem anderen Sportwagen fahren so viel Magie und Mythos mit wie in den feuerroten Ikonen aus Maranello. Wo die Autos mit dem springenden Pferd im Wappen starten, stehen sie stets im Mittelpunkt. Car History zeigt die Geschichte der roten Renner aus Maranello, dazu historische Aufnahmen aus der Formel 1 und O-Töne von Michael Schumacher.

programme.title: Rückspiegel
programme.desc: Ein halbes Jahrhundert Ferrari. Rückspiegel geht dem Mythos Ferrari auf den Grund und nimmt die roten Renner aus Maranello unter die Lupe.

programme.title: Rückspiegel
programme.desc: 1997 feierte Ferrari den 50. Firmen-Geburtstag. Wolfgang Rother ging damals dem Ferrari-Mythos nach und sammelte erste Fahreindrücke mit dem Ferrari 550 Maranello.

programme.title: Aston Martin Rapide S - Kraftvoll, stilvoll, dynamisch
programme.desc: Kraftvoll, stilvoll, dynamisch und trotzem geraumig. Der Aston Martin Rapide S tanzt bei der für Zweitürer bekannten Marke voll aus der Reihe. Bleibt er den Grundsatzen der Marke damit treu? Motorvision klart auf.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: Auf der Retro Classic in Stuttgart, wo sich Gründer Karl-Ulrich Herrmann nach 20 erfolgreichen Jahren verabschiedet, sucht Top Speed-Moderator Martin Utberg nach der Antwort auf die Frage, ob Oldtimer eine Zukunft haben.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.sub-title: Zu Gast am Salzburgring und in Stuttgart
programme.desc: In dieser Sendung schauen wir uns an, wie ein BMW 3.0 CS gescannt wird, um schließlich ein Modellfahruzeug daraus zu machen, wir schauen uns Österreichs grösste Rennserie - den Histo Cup - mit Graf Christian von Wedel und seinem Sohn Lando näher an, der schon Erfolde ist in dieser Serie gefeiert hat.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: In dieser Folge besucht Top Speed-Moderator Martin Utberg die Oldtimer Gallery Toffen in der Schweiz, wo er einen Kurs zum Auktionator absolviert, zwei spezielle Oldtimer fährt und eine der wenigen weiblichen Mechanikerinnen der Oldtimer-Szene trifft.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: Top-Speed-Moderator Martin Utberg gibt einen Blick hinter die Kulissen der Seefeld Classic Tour. Sie können sehen, was zur Organisation eines Oldtimer-Events erforderlich ist, wie die Routen erstellt werden und wie die Teilnehmer das Event letztendlich erleben.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: Top-Speed-Moderator Martin Utberg nimmt an der 9 Seen Tour teil, eine Oldtimerveranstaltung, die am Tegernsee beginnt und endet. Während dieser Veranstaltung fährt Martin ein sehr spezielles Auto. Martin ist auch Moderator bei einer Online-Wohltätigkeitsauktion zugunsten der Lebenshilfe Berchtesgadenerland und zeigt den speziellen Mercedes 320 A, mit dem er auf dem Weg zum Auktionshaus ist.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: In diesem Top Speed Classic Special empfängt Moderator Martin Utberg den ehemaligen F1-Fahrer Jochen Mass im wunderschönen 5-Sterne-Hotel Klosterbräu in Seefeld in Tirol. Und spricht mit ihm auf sehr persönliche Weise über seine Karriere und über sein Privatleben. Der Zuschauer lernt die philosophische Legende aus einem ganz anderen Blickwinkel kennen.

programme.title: Vom „Schrotthaufen“ zur echten Rarität: Die einzigartige Geschichte des Porsche 911 ST 2,5
programme.desc: Einer der seltenen Porsche der frühen 70er Jahre - der 911 2,5 oder ST, wie er auch genannt wird. Das war eine Kleinserie, eine Rennsportvariante des Elfers. 980 kg leicht, 270 PS aus 2,5 Liter Hubraum und wahnsinnig schnell. Es gibt nur noch ganz wenige.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Mit der Studie 'Alfieri' hat sich Maserati ein traumhaft gezeichnetes Coupé zu seinem 100. Geburtstag geschenkt. Supercars stellt den neuen Ghibli SQ4 vor, blickt zurück auf die faszinierendsten Modelle der traditionsreichen Marke und zeigt die aktuellen Modelle. Auto alla italiana, dolce vita auf vier Rädern.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Sind die Kinder hinten raus, kann der Papa ordentlich Gas geben. Der Audi S8 und der Jaguar XF-RS Sportbrake garantieren mit weit über 500 PS extremen Fahrspaß bei gediegenen Platzverhältnissen. Der eine mehr dem Luxus verbunden, der andere mehr dem Sport.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Nur wenige Sportwagen üben die Faszination eines McLaren aus und blicken zurück auf eine legendäre Vergangenheit im Motorsport. Zwei Modelle hat McLaren im Programm. Den 650S, Nachfolger des MP4 12C und den limitierten Supersportler P1. Supercars gibt sich der Faszination des 650 S hin.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Die Hersteller von Sportwagen und Luxuslimousinen stehen ja schon lange nicht mehr im Verdacht mit Leistung zu geizen. Aber genug genügt manchen nicht, und so gibt es einen Markt, auf dem selbst Hochleistungsfahrzeuge zu weiterer Leistung getrieben werden. Zwei extreme Beispiele: Japan. Land der Extreme: Extrem konservativ, extrem modern, extrem schrill. Nissan jagt mit dem neuen GTR wieder Sorgenfalten auf die Stirn europäischer Sportwagenhersteller. Keiner von ihnen ist in der Lage zu einem Preis von weniger als 100.000 Euro einen 550 PS Allradsupersportler auf den Markt zu bringen, der in 3 Sekunden die 100 durchbricht, und auf dem Nürburgring Topzeiten hinlegt. Supercars gibt Gas.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Wenn es quer geht und das Heck raucht, ist die Traktion am Limit und der Spaß groß. Supercars geht Driften und spart Geld. Denn quer fahren muss nicht extrem teuer sein. Der BMW M 235i RS und der Subaru BRZ sind zwei Spielzeuge der Wahl für das Kind im Drift-Mann.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Wenn's der Papa eilig hat ... Kombis über 500 PS sind eigentlich Wahnsinn! Aber gebaut werden Sie trotzdem. Und es macht auch richtig Spaß sie zu bewegen. Das leistungsstärkste Serienmodell auf dem Markt ist im Moment der E63 S AMG mit 585 PS. Supercars testet den Überkombi und vergleicht ihn mit seiner Konkurrenz.

programme.title: Ferrari FF
programme.desc: Der Ferrari FF ist ein idealer Familien-Sportwagen für alle Jahreszeiten. Rennwagen und Kombi - besser hat die beiden Gegensatze noch keiner vereint. Interessant, dass dies gerade Ferrari gelingt. Und schön ist der FF auch noch - einfach eine 'Bella macchina'.

programme.title: Abenteuer Allrad
programme.desc: Wir haben die Vorbereitungen der Teams von Volkswagen und BMW auf die Rallye Dakar in Südamerika begleitet. Außerdem: Wir waren mit dem Mitsubishi F200 in Norwegen. Und: der BMW X6 M auf unserer Teststrecke.

programme.title: Abenteuer Allrad
programme.desc: Wir präsentieren die Ergebnisse unseres Dauertests des Land Rover Discovery. Und: Wir ließen den Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution gegen das BMW 135i Coupé, den Volkswagen R36 und den Subaru Impreza WRX antreten.

programme.title: Abenteuer Allrad
programme.desc: Wir nehmen Sie mit nach Lappland in Schweden zum exklusiven Winterfahrertraining von AMG für den Mercedes-AMG C63. Und: das Finale der German Offroad Masters auf dem Nürburgring.

programme.title: Abenteuer Allrad
programme.desc: Wir haben die Teilnehmer der Land Rover Experience Tour Asia begleitet. Und: Der erste SUV von Dacia, der Duster.

programme.title: Abenteuer Allrad
programme.desc: Sportwagen oder Familienkutsche? Fußballtrainer Jürgen Klopp testet den Mitsubishi Lancer Sportback in Lissabon. Und: Wir waren mit dem Mercedes-Benz GL in Island.

programme.title: Mercedes S63 AMG Cabrio: Ein Frischluft-Luxusliner für die Reichen
programme.desc: Die Mercedes S-Klasse: Das Statussymbol der Reichen und Schönen. Seit 1991 bringt Mercedes wieder ein Cabriolet auf den Markt. Was es drauf hat, hat Motorvision getestet.

programme.title: Besser als der CLA Shootingbreak? - Kia ProCeed & Kia Ceed GT
programme.desc: Kia bringt mit dem neuen ProCeed einen eleganten Shooting Brake! Einzige Konkurrenz: Der Mercedes CLA Shooting Brake. Will Kia ernsthaft Mercedes angreifen? Leiden die Koreaner jetzt an völliger Selbstüberschatzung, oder ist er am Ende sogar der bessere Shooting Brake?

programme.title: Put your car on TV
programme.desc: Nirgendwo auf der Welt gibt es so viele Auto-Verrückte wie in Dubai. Und nirgendwo in Dubai ist das Aufkommen an abgedrehten, aufgemotzten oder getunten Luxusschlitten und Supercars so hoch, wie auf "The Walk", dem Pracht-Boulevard des Jumeirah Beach. Nur einen Steinwurf (weit weg) von "The Palm", präsentieren die beiden Hosts Mylene Gomera und Saif Hattawi vor der Kulisse des Sofitel Dubai Jumeirah Beach mit "Put your Car on TV" Social-TV á la Dubai. Sehen und gesehen werden für die Scheichs unter den Auto-Nerds.

programme.title: Rimac Concept One: Der schnellste Elektro-Supersportler der Welt
programme.desc: Ein Supersportler der in 2,8 Sekunden die 100 Km/h knackt, muss nicht immer ein Verbrenner sein. Im Concept One von Rimac, erreichen insgesamt 4 Elektromotoren eine unfassbare Leistung von 1088 PS und 1600 Newtonmeter Drehmoment.

programme.title: Audi E-Tron GT
programme.desc: Mit dem Audi e-tron GT hat Audi einen Meilenstein gesetzt, auch wenn er mit dem Porsche Taycan verwandt ist, die Ingolstädter haben hier eine eigene Duftmarke in Sachen Zukunft gesetzt. Die reinen Zahlen sagen schon alles. Das Einstiegsmodell leistet 476 PS, die Topversion sogar bis zu 646 PS!

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: Aus der Liebe zum Motorsport ist alles entstanden', war das Motto von Paul Pietsch. Und das gilt auch für die Paul Pietsch Classic, die an den im Alter von 100 Jahren verstorbenen Rennfahrer und Verleger erinnert. Bei der achten Ausgabe der Rallye im Schwarzwald gehen 116 Autos an den Start. Mit dabei ist auch Martin Utberg.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: In einem historischen Fiat Spider durch die wunderschöne Landschaft rund um das österreichische Salzburg fahren: Das ist ein Traum für jeden Oldtimer-Enthusiasten. Für Top-Speed-Moderator Martin Utberg wird dieser Traum Wirklichkeit, als er zusammen mit dem Schweizer Rallyeenthusiast Sven Wolter am Gaisbergrennen teilnimmt. Auf dem Programm stehen der City Grand Prix, ein Besuch am Salzburger Ring und eine schwierige Wertungsprüfung am Gaisberg.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: Seit 2000 findet in und um Bad Kissingen in der Nähe von Schweinfurt die Sachs Franken Classic statt. Die Teilnehmer legen bei der Oldtimer-Rallye über zwei Tage etwa 550 Kilometer zurück und müssen im Fränkischen Weinland, dem Spessart, den Steigerwald und weiteren Orten rund 20 Prüfungen absolvieren. 2019 ist Martin Utberg zum zweiten Mal unter den Teilnehmern der Sachs Franken Classic.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: Der Altmühltal Classic Sprint ist ein Gleichmäßigkeitsrennen für historische Automobile. Die dreitägige Oldtimerrallye wird einmal jährlich in Nürnberg gestartet, führt quer durch Mittelfranken und am zweiten Tag durch das malerische Altmühltal. Das Veranstaltungsmotto lautet 'Von Freunden für Freunde'. Top-Speed-Moderator Martin Utberg ist zusammen mit Teampartner Thomas Voglar am Steuer eines einzigartigen Daimler SP 250 dabei.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: Die Edelweiß Classic ist die dreitägige Kultrallye durch das Voralpenland, die nicht nur auf der Straße viel bewegt. Neben der entspannten Ausfahrt durch die Region um Berchtesgarden steht nämlich auch der soziale Aspekt im Mittelpunkt der Rallye: Der gesamte Erlös kommt Menschen mit Behinderung zugute. Martin Utberg ist zusammen mit seinem Partner Michael Steenhuis in einem Porsche 911 Carrera Targa aus 1986 am Start.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: Auch 2019 ist die Silvretta Classic ein Gipfeltreffen automobiler Schätze. Wo sonst könnte die Herausforderung für Mensch und Material, für die Pioniere von damals und heute größer sein, als auf den herrlichen Pass-Strecken der österreichischen Alpen. Top-Speed-Moderator Martin Utberg nimmt die Herausforderung auch in diesem Jahr wieder an.

programme.title: Top Speed Classic
programme.desc: 2019 findet die Oberbayerische Meister Classic der Kfz-Innung München-Oberbayern zum sechsten Mal statt. Wie in den Vorjahren haben die Veranstalter auch in diesem Jahr wieder einen neuen Austragungsort ausgewählt. So findet die Rallye, die mit dem Fokus auf das Miteinander konzipiert ist, in diesem Jahr in und um das malerische Altmühltal statt.

programme.title: Facel Vega Facellia - Traumwagen und Kultklassiker
programme.desc: Traumwagen und Kultklassiker aus Frankreich. Der Facel Vega Facellia, schön wie eine französische Filmdiva, aber auch genauso zickig.

programme.title: VW Karmann Ghia RS: Explosive Mixtur aus Volkswagen- und Porscheteilen
programme.desc: Man nehme eine schnittige Volkswagenhülle und pumpe sie voll mit Porsche-Technik. Genau das hat Jochen Bader mit seinem Karmann Ghia von 1970 getan. Ein Klassik-Hybride der absolut besonderen Art.

programme.title: Audi Quattro - Der Rallye-Klassiker
programme.desc: Vorsprung durch Technik auf der Rallyepiste. Der Audi Quattro schockiert seine Gegner.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Mit der Studie 'Alfieri' hat sich Maserati ein traumhaft gezeichnetes Coupé zu seinem 100. Geburtstag geschenkt. Supercars stellt den neuen Ghibli SQ4 vor, blickt zurück auf die faszinierendsten Modelle der traditionsreichen Marke und zeigt die aktuellen Modelle. Auto alla italiana, dolce vita auf vier Rädern.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Sind die Kinder hinten raus, kann der Papa ordentlich Gas geben. Der Audi S8 und der Jaguar XF-RS Sportbrake garantieren mit weit über 500 PS extremen Fahrspaß bei gediegenen Platzverhältnissen. Der eine mehr dem Luxus verbunden, der andere mehr dem Sport.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Nur wenige Sportwagen üben die Faszination eines McLaren aus und blicken zurück auf eine legendäre Vergangenheit im Motorsport. Zwei Modelle hat McLaren im Programm. Den 650S, Nachfolger des MP4 12C und den limitierten Supersportler P1. Supercars gibt sich der Faszination des 650 S hin.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Die Hersteller von Sportwagen und Luxuslimousinen stehen ja schon lange nicht mehr im Verdacht mit Leistung zu geizen. Aber genug genügt manchen nicht, und so gibt es einen Markt, auf dem selbst Hochleistungsfahrzeuge zu weiterer Leistung getrieben werden. Zwei extreme Beispiele: Japan. Land der Extreme: Extrem konservativ, extrem modern, extrem schrill. Nissan jagt mit dem neuen GTR wieder Sorgenfalten auf die Stirn europäischer Sportwagenhersteller. Keiner von ihnen ist in der Lage zu einem Preis von weniger als 100.000 Euro einen 550 PS Allradsupersportler auf den Markt zu bringen, der in 3 Sekunden die 100 durchbricht, und auf dem Nürburgring Topzeiten hinlegt. Supercars gibt Gas.

programme.title: Supercars
programme.desc: Wenn es quer geht und das Heck raucht, ist die Traktion am Limit und der Spaß groß. Supercars geht Driften und spart Geld. Denn quer fahren muss nicht extrem teuer sein. Der BMW M 235i RS und der Subaru BRZ sind zwei Spielzeuge der Wahl für das Kind im Drift-Mann.

programme.title: The Outpost
programme.desc: After summoning Zed and other Blackbloods to save the Outpost, Talon is caught between loyalty to her friends and her Blackblood heritage. A Priestess named Yavalla promises a Blackblood paradise and teaches Talon about her lost family. But when a mind-numbing epidemic consumes the Realm, Talon must solve the mystery of her past and unleash a forgotten power before the world is forever enslaved.

Talon must awaken the powers lying dormant in her dark blood and make true friends at the Outpost to lead a rebellion against the regime.

programme.title: mareTV: Estonia's Enchanted Islands - Kihnu, Hiiumaa, Saaremaa & Co
programme.desc: Kihnu is one of 19 inhabited Estonian islands. When the women there ride motorcycles in colourful skirts, it is summer. Thanks to its remoteness, charming traditions have been preserved here. More than 2,000 islands belong to Estonia, none is like the other, each with its own character. Most of them were military restricted areas during the Soviet Union. Of all things, the strict shielding had its good points: beach, forest, juniper groves, they still characterise the landscape of Estonia's enchanted islands. Elly Karjam is a "multi-jobber": lighthouse keeper, ice-cream producer and contract knitter for the famous Kihnu sweaters. Summer is high season for her: She is expecting guests from the USA, who had their ancestors on Kihnu. Birches have to be cut for the so-called viht. This bunch of birch branches is an important accessory for the traditional sauna at midsummer. And the motorcycles in the shed are to be refloated.

programme.title: Symphony of the Seas - Underwater Wonders of Australia's Ocean
programme.desc: Our journeys take us all around the world from Patagonia to the USA, from Greenland to South Africa and from Cambodia to Australia and leads us to the most fascinating places where landscapes animals and humans are the main focus of our documentaries. Whether on land or at sea – the last paradises of the world are our destination.

programme.title: Secrets of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: The contours of the Mediterranean have changed during the course of its history. Near Gibraltar, Africa was once connected to the European continent. When the land bridge at Gibraltar collapsed, the Mediterranean basin filled up again. The Suez Canal is today connected to the Red Sea. This route enables animals to reach the Mediterranean, where they cause problems.

programme.title: Secrets of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Rugged rocks, blue sea and idyllic, sandy beaches - this is the Mediterranean as we know it. But this impression is deceptive: the Mediterranean is under constant change. The continents are moving towards one another. Animals, that have to survive under such extreme conditions, must find a way to escape the dangers. Between deserts and volcanoes, the challenges for the animals are enormous.

programme.title: Northern Woods
programme.desc: It is a musical film a a tributeto the Nordic forest: it shows its development from a primeval wood to a cultivated forest. Once populated by wild animals such as wolves, bears, eagles, deer and musk oxen, complex re-enactment-scenes shot by dollies and helicopters vividly depict the colonization of the forest by the Celts and Germans. But as time progressed, the northern forest has on numerous occasions fallen victim to environmental degradation and overexploitation. Several provisions were made to protect this wild beauty. The Helsinki resolution of 1993, which stipulated that the woods be used in a way and in a magnitude which guarantees their biological variety and productiveness and vitality, is but one measure put in place to secure the preservation of the natural gem. Time-lapse photography and breath-taking shots show our main protagonist – the woods – in its stunning glory. This beautiful wooded land, changes throughout the seasons. Our woodland is a world-renowned ecological jewel. It is famous, well-known and loved by tourists, forest economists, environmentalists, historians and intellectuals alike.

programme.title: Lobsters - The Knights Of The Deep
programme.desc: The knights of the deep are on the move; almost no part of their bodies is without armor. Like medieval warriors, these fighters are well armed – not with sword and shield, but with scissors and forceps and defensive armor that is covered with spikes and hooks. And even though they are well protected and have an uncanny awareness of their surroundings, many of these proud knights will face a gloomy destiny. Many of them will end upon a plate. Gourmets all over the world are in love with these famous crustaceans: lobsters! For marine biologists lobsters are similarly fascinating: as research objects. We are on their trail in Cape Breton, an island in the northern Atlantic and part of the Canadian province Nova Scotia, where one of the largest populations of lobsters has its home.

programme.title: Chasing Quakes
programme.desc: Europe has experienced catastrophic earthquakes – even though the 'old continent' is not the most notorious region on Earth for strong quakes, the danger from below is very real. Autumn 2016 tragedy strikes north-central Italy. A series of four earthquakes cracks a mountain and flattens a historic town.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: It is a road of mountain passes and India’s access to the roof of the world – the Himalayas. This 475-kilometre long route at the northernmost tip of the Indian subcontinent connects the cities of Manali and Leh at the heart of the Ladakh region. The term “highway” applies quite literally, since the route traverses five of the highest drivable mountain passes in the world – among these the Lohtang La at 3,978 metres above sea level, the Lachulung La at 5,059 metres and the Tanglang La at 5,325 metres. Crossing these passes is a challenge for both vehicle and man. The mountain peaks, still snow-capped even in the depths of summer, wide variety of vegetation and the fantastic and craggy landscape turn any journey into a captivating adventure.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: In Bangladesh, the land with the highest density of population in the world (and the highest amount of corruption), the daily struggle to survive is fought everywhere, including the streets. Nowhere do people drive as brutally and recklessly as here. In Bangladesh you drive on the road like others drive with a bumper car: if you need space, you simply ram the car driving next to you. The police only came if there are fatalities. The biggest bottleneck in the transport system is the historical old town of Dhaka. Old Dhaka is a universe of its own, a world of bazaars in which every trade has its own quarter: there are streets of jewelers, sweets makers and fashionable tailors, and the vegetable wholesalers have their warehouses down at the port. The deliveries take place mostly on the river, the Buriganga River, a stinking cesspool. But the sold goods usually leave by land, and the customers also come by the land route – the Nawabpur Road. They generally come in buses or by rickshaw, where too many people are crammed into too little space. The traffic in Dhaka is everyday, normal madness. The film accompanies a rickshaw, a bus and a truck on their dangerous way through the streets of Dhaka and shows how it is possible to survive in what seems to be an incontrollable chaos.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The “Adriatic Highway” is one of the most beautiful coastal roads in the world. The “technical masterwork” was built in the 1950s and 60s, at the time of Yugoslavian President Tito. Abounding in curves, the asphalt road stretches from Ankaran in Slovenia to Ulcinj in Montenegro. More than half of the road is in Croatia (659 km) and a quarter in Montenegro (125 km). Shorter segments lead through Slovenia; only nine kilometers are in Bosnia and Herzegovina. For all four countries of the former Yugoslavian Federation, the 1,200-kilometer-long highway remains the main thoroughfare of Adriatic tourism. For many travelers, the highway is the absolute dream road. In dizzying heights, it hugs the steep cliffs lining the Adriatic Sea, winds through coves and bays, gardens and stony fields. Wonderful views of the blue sea, green islands, bizarre cliffs and Mediterranean cities and towns are typical of the highway. But with its numerous curves, the dream road also harbors many dangers.

programme.title: mareTV: Madeira - Portugal's sea of blossoms in the Atlantic Ocean
programme.desc: Flower magic in Madeira: The Flower Festival Festa da Flor is the most important event of the year for the people of the Atlantic island. With it they celebrate spring, which is climatically practically all year round here, their island and themselves. The coast formed by lava, centuries-old laurel forests and green steep slopes make Madeira unique. Those who start right at the front of the big parade of the flower festival in the capital Funchal, will have made it. For Isabel Borges this dream has come true. She opens this year's flower parade along the harbour promenade with her festive group. This accolade does not only mean fame and prestige, but also a lot of pressure. Are the self-designed dresses splendid enough? Will the 150 flower children learn the dance steps in time? Will the flowers on the float hold out in the heat? For Isabel, it is now a matter of nerves.

programme.title: mareTV: La Palma: The Greenest of the Canaries
programme.desc: Thundering waterfalls, ancient forests and an impressive volcanic landscape with black beaches: La Palma is a dream island for nature lovers. It is by far the island of the Canary Islands with the most green, almost half of it is covered with forest. But once a year the green island is dominated by the color white. On Rosenmontag (Rose Monday), the inhabitants have for decades been targeting those ancestors who returned from abroad wealthy and ostentatiously demonstrated their wealth with powdered faces. The carnivalistic approach culminates every year in a white chaos, with tons of talcum, flour or paint trickling down the uniformly white dressed islanders. On the Roque de los Muchachos, La Palma's highest mountain at 2,400 meters, stands one of the largest reflecting telescopes in the world. Astrophysicists love the island because it is the perfect place to look into space. Researchers and star lovers look spellbound to Beteigeuze. The giant star is probably in front of a supernova and could become a second moon in the firmament.

programme.title: Giants of Fortune - The Whale Sharks of Oslob
programme.desc: In the little Filipino village of Oslob on the Cebu Island, people suffer from typhoons and overfishing. Until the world’s biggest fish and the Internet change everything.Fisherman Zosimo’s dearest wish is for his children to graduate from high school one day. Yet the chance that this wish will come true is tiny, since at times Zosimo doesn’t even manage to feed the family. Typhoons and overfishing make the lives of Oslob fishermen difficult.

programme.title: The marvellous World of French Rivers
programme.desc: The Gironde is the largest and most powerful tidal current in Europe. When the Gironde flows into the Atlantic, it is 15 kilometers wide and in the rhythm of the tides, it brings the waters from the Pyrenees and the Massif Central into the ocean. This often pushes its waters far out into the Gironde at high tide.This creates a world of its own that has shaped everything uniquely and intensely for tens of thousands of years. The water surface of the river is so large that the evaporation has created its own microclimate, which is stable and, together with the brackish waters, has influenced flora and fauna on the right and left of the bank for a long time.

programme.title: The marvellous World of French Rivers
programme.desc: The Dordogne consists of a visible and an invisible system of flowing water. Caves and basins under the earth's surface store the excess water and return it to the river when it is dry. A perfect management of a precious resource, not invented by humans, but by the complex nature itself. The result is an ever life-giving river.

programme.title: mareTV: Jersey - Sunshine Island in the English Channel
programme.desc: Jersey: the Channel Island is one of the areas in the UK that can boast the most hours of annual sunshine. Not that Dave Cowburn cares very much. He works in the dark, cool ducts of an old bunker from the Sec-ond World War. Here, he breeds turbot, and is very successful at it, too. The "Jersey Royal", the regal potato, has been grown on the island since 1880, fertilized with seaweed from the surrounding ocean. In the third generation, Christine Hellio manages approximately 20 hectares on the coast. "The potato is our most important export commodity", she says. It is harvested by hand, as machines cannot be used on the steep fields. The price is quite regal, too: One kilogram costs 6 Euros. Hugh Gill is one of around 240 voluntary police officers on Jersey. The Honorary Police is regarded as the oldest organised police system in the world. Hugh works for them for one week every month. On the green lanes, the streets of Jersey, the speed limit is 15 miles per hour. Jersey has an immense tidal range and with up to 13 metres difference, it is the world's third largest. This is good for a rarity: the Ormer - one of the world's most expensive species of snail.

programme.title: The Provence coast - Marseille and the Côte Bleue
programme.desc: The Provence is famed for its endless fields of laven-der, but this lush landscape also has a beautifully mari-time touch: The Côte Bleue! Small, hidden beaches, charming harbour towns, imposing, craggy bays and a uniquely clear light that has attracted painters includ-ing Cézanne and Braque. The coast derives its name from the deep blue water and extends from Marseille to Martigues. This small town is also known as "The Ven-ice of the North", as it is shaped entirely by water: an inland lake, the sea itself, as well as a connecting canal. In the bays of the Calanques, the steeply-walled coastal inlets in the Mediterranean limestone, Lionel Franc is a cliff diver. His personal record is a hight of 36 metres! Ambi is a sculptress. This young artist's work, who moved to Marseille from Madagascar many years ago, is characterised by a dynamic momentum. As a pas-sionate pétanque player, she demonstrates this drive on the boules courts of the port city. John Pendray is Pein-tre officiel de la Marine, an official marine painter. The French state allows just 40 painters to its circle. There are no monetary rewards, but heaps of honour and a very smart uniform!

programme.title: Eyes Of The Atacama
programme.desc: ALMA – the Atacama Large Millimeter Array – is the ultimate space observation facility. Here, 66 leviathan parabolic antennae trap cosmic rays in the previously unobservable long-wave range. It can only happen in Atacama, far away from civilisation’s pollution of the night sky with artificial light.

programme.title: Tren Atlantico
programme.desc: We travel by train from the westernmost point of mainland Europe up to Portugal's only national park, the Peneda-Gerês, and from lively Porto to the Spanish border in the northeast. The train takes you from the blue sea to the green Douro Valley, from the urban metropolis to the scorching heat of the deserted hinterland.

programme.title: Tren Atlantico
programme.desc: Switzerland or Spain? This question is often asked by those who see pictures from northern Spain for the first time: High mountains, lonely villages, but - this is the crucial difference - also breathtaking Atlantic beaches. The "Costa Verde", the green coast, is a piece of Spain that is so different from the general tourist image of the Germans' favorite vacation destination. This area has been spared from mass tourism. We travel by train from Bilbao in the Basque Country to Santander in Cantabria and Asturias.

programme.title: Germany's Wild Amazon
programme.desc: As one of Germany’s beauties, the river was the gem of Germanys landscape. But with industrialization it became the country’s hardest working river and like everything that has been overworked, it lost it magnificence and charm. Due to tender love and care, the river is now a reigning example of one of the most successful and outstanding renaturation projects in the country.The film shows never before seen shots of the river now pulsing with life. We will show you the winding river bed, spawning salmon, mating crabs and still-growing anchor ice. You will see dipper birds searching for food under water, kingfishers catching fish, a family life of badgers, foxes and a wide variety of birds. Come and meet the resurrected river Wupper!

programme.title: Germany's Wild Reservoirs
programme.desc: One of the smallest dams in the Bergisches Land is the Panzertalsperre, with an area of just four-and-a-half football pitches. On the other hand, the Dhünntalsperre is the largest with the area of 660 football pitches. They all transform a stretch of flowing water into still and stagnant water. As a result, completely diverse ecosystems have developed there: where the dipper once dived for insect larvae, cormorants and gray herons now fish and swans and coots cavort. In recent summers, even greater challenges have emerged: the effects of climate change - from extreme drought to destructive floods. On a smaller scale, a rather industrious dam master is operating flood protection: The Beaver. However, the water masses of the Wupper tore away half of his majestic timber castle - and the four young beaver kids were not seen again afterwards. Have they survived the flood? Not everyone can cope with the constant change in the dams, but they still remain an important wonder of engineering for many: for us humans as well as for a number of animals. By combining water management, ecological requirements and tourism a worthwhile goal is possible: Because for the Bergisches Land, its dams are among the most valuable and popular infrastructures that the region has to offer.

programme.title: The Sun - Inferno in the Sky
programme.desc: On July 23rd, 2012, a massive eruption on the sun hurls a colossal cloud of solar matter into space. It’s the most severe sunstorm in 150 years. Fortunately, the Earth is not in the direct path of this solar ejection. But it’s only a matter of time before a violent solar storm hits us. When these clouds of charged matter reach our planet, they can wreak havoc in electrical systems.

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Roads are more than just gray strips of asphalt that allow us to travel and trade. For centuries they have been lifelines of mankind, full of stories and history - and in certain countries and areas they also hold great dangers, much human suffering and death. Documentary filmmaker Oliver G. Becker ventured onto the dangerous roads of Afghanistan's Hindu Kush Mountains, the infamous Moloto Road in South Africa, along the vertiginous slopes of the Bolivian Andes and other "roads of death" in India, Georgia and the Ivory Coast

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Some risks on these autoroutes have natural causes: Extreme weather, avalanches and landslides. In some areas, the locals even believe that evil spirits kill travelers. But many of the dangers are man-made: robbers or terrorists lie in wait for travelers, and tough labor pressures, social hardship and greedy mass-transit businesses also cause tragic driving accidents around the world. In the 20th century alone, 35 million people died on roads worldwide - plus 1.5 billion injured! With the two-part "Death Roads - On the Road at the Limit," phoenix offers a documentary road movie along the world's most dangerous car routes.

programme.title: Menorca - Majorca's beautiful sister
programme.desc: Not nearly as crowded as Majorca or Ibiza: Menorca has noticeably fewer visitors than her sister islands and in 1993, was recognised by UNESCO as a biosphere re-serve. Menorca also has its own distinctive charm, with its secluded coves, mighty cliffs, beautiful gardens and ages old towns and villages. Its residents love the is-lands treasures and peculiarities. Forests make up al-most a third of Menorca, complemented by many lush green meadows. Next to tourism, agriculture is a major source of the island's income to the present day. On Menorca, there are several accumulations of enormous megalithic stones. From a global point of view, the up to five-metre-tall "Taulas", whereby the stones are ar-ranged in the shape of a "T", are unique.

programme.title: Wild Sardinia
programme.desc: Sardinia has always been the epitome of pure wilderness, an emerald of volcanic origin in the Mediterranean. 1900 metres of coastline and an infinite maze of offshore islands. But Sardinia also has other facets: green valleys, rugged mountains, murmuring brooks, mysterious ruins and a unique fauna. Just off of Sardinia's coast is an untouched underwater paradise - uniquely beautiful, but also dangerous. Pilot whales, dolphins and mobula rays populate the waters at Capo Testa in the north of the island. In the west, the lagoons of Cabras represent a wild landscape of lakes in which thousands of flamingos live and hunt the red brine shrimps. In addition to the flamingos, grey and purple herons and little egrets breed here. Thousands of bats have found refuge in the craggy mountain world of the Supramonte and Gennargentu, with their countless grottoes and caves. In the sea we can observe the mass mating of sea slugs, and thanks to our camera robots and submersible boats we were able to observe beard worms with luminous red gills, as well as bright yellow tree corals in the area surrounding the hypothermal lava holes.

programme.title: mareTV: Estonia's Enchanted Islands - Kihnu, Hiiumaa, Saaremaa & Co
programme.desc: Kihnu is one of 19 inhabited Estonian islands. When the women there ride motorcycles in colourful skirts, it is summer. Thanks to its remoteness, charming traditions have been preserved here. More than 2,000 islands belong to Estonia, none is like the other, each with its own character. Most of them were military restricted areas during the Soviet Union. Of all things, the strict shielding had its good points: beach, forest, juniper groves, they still characterise the landscape of Estonia's enchanted islands. Elly Karjam is a "multi-jobber": lighthouse keeper, ice-cream producer and contract knitter for the famous Kihnu sweaters. Summer is high season for her: She is expecting guests from the USA, who had their ancestors on Kihnu. Birches have to be cut for the so-called viht. This bunch of birch branches is an important accessory for the traditional sauna at midsummer. And the motorcycles in the shed are to be refloated.

programme.title: Symphony of the Seas - Underwater Wonders of Australia's Ocean
programme.desc: Our journeys take us all around the world from Patagonia to the USA, from Greenland to South Africa and from Cambodia to Australia and leads us to the most fascinating places where landscapes animals and humans are the main focus of our documentaries. Whether on land or at sea – the last paradises of the world are our destination.

programme.title: Secrets of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: The contours of the Mediterranean have changed during the course of its history. Near Gibraltar, Africa was once connected to the European continent. When the land bridge at Gibraltar collapsed, the Mediterranean basin filled up again. The Suez Canal is today connected to the Red Sea. This route enables animals to reach the Mediterranean, where they cause problems.

programme.title: Secrets of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Rugged rocks, blue sea and idyllic, sandy beaches - this is the Mediterranean as we know it. But this impression is deceptive: the Mediterranean is under constant change. The continents are moving towards one another. Animals, that have to survive under such extreme conditions, must find a way to escape the dangers. Between deserts and volcanoes, the challenges for the animals are enormous.

programme.title: Northern Woods
programme.desc: It is a musical film a a tributeto the Nordic forest: it shows its development from a primeval wood to a cultivated forest. Once populated by wild animals such as wolves, bears, eagles, deer and musk oxen, complex re-enactment-scenes shot by dollies and helicopters vividly depict the colonization of the forest by the Celts and Germans. But as time progressed, the northern forest has on numerous occasions fallen victim to environmental degradation and overexploitation. Several provisions were made to protect this wild beauty. The Helsinki resolution of 1993, which stipulated that the woods be used in a way and in a magnitude which guarantees their biological variety and productiveness and vitality, is but one measure put in place to secure the preservation of the natural gem. Time-lapse photography and breath-taking shots show our main protagonist – the woods – in its stunning glory. This beautiful wooded land, changes throughout the seasons. Our woodland is a world-renowned ecological jewel. It is famous, well-known and loved by tourists, forest economists, environmentalists, historians and intellectuals alike.

programme.title: Lobsters - The Knights Of The Deep
programme.desc: The knights of the deep are on the move; almost no part of their bodies is without armor. Like medieval warriors, these fighters are well armed – not with sword and shield, but with scissors and forceps and defensive armor that is covered with spikes and hooks. And even though they are well protected and have an uncanny awareness of their surroundings, many of these proud knights will face a gloomy destiny. Many of them will end upon a plate. Gourmets all over the world are in love with these famous crustaceans: lobsters! For marine biologists lobsters are similarly fascinating: as research objects. We are on their trail in Cape Breton, an island in the northern Atlantic and part of the Canadian province Nova Scotia, where one of the largest populations of lobsters has its home.

programme.title: Chasing Quakes
programme.desc: Europe has experienced catastrophic earthquakes – even though the 'old continent' is not the most notorious region on Earth for strong quakes, the danger from below is very real. Autumn 2016 tragedy strikes north-central Italy. A series of four earthquakes cracks a mountain and flattens a historic town.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: It is a road of mountain passes and India’s access to the roof of the world – the Himalayas. This 475-kilometre long route at the northernmost tip of the Indian subcontinent connects the cities of Manali and Leh at the heart of the Ladakh region. The term “highway” applies quite literally, since the route traverses five of the highest drivable mountain passes in the world – among these the Lohtang La at 3,978 metres above sea level, the Lachulung La at 5,059 metres and the Tanglang La at 5,325 metres. Crossing these passes is a challenge for both vehicle and man. The mountain peaks, still snow-capped even in the depths of summer, wide variety of vegetation and the fantastic and craggy landscape turn any journey into a captivating adventure.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: In Bangladesh, the land with the highest density of population in the world (and the highest amount of corruption), the daily struggle to survive is fought everywhere, including the streets. Nowhere do people drive as brutally and recklessly as here. In Bangladesh you drive on the road like others drive with a bumper car: if you need space, you simply ram the car driving next to you. The police only came if there are fatalities. The biggest bottleneck in the transport system is the historical old town of Dhaka. Old Dhaka is a universe of its own, a world of bazaars in which every trade has its own quarter: there are streets of jewelers, sweets makers and fashionable tailors, and the vegetable wholesalers have their warehouses down at the port. The deliveries take place mostly on the river, the Buriganga River, a stinking cesspool. But the sold goods usually leave by land, and the customers also come by the land route – the Nawabpur Road. They generally come in buses or by rickshaw, where too many people are crammed into too little space. The traffic in Dhaka is everyday, normal madness. The film accompanies a rickshaw, a bus and a truck on their dangerous way through the streets of Dhaka and shows how it is possible to survive in what seems to be an incontrollable chaos.

programme.title: Hot Roads - The Worlds Most Dangerous Roads
programme.desc: The “Adriatic Highway” is one of the most beautiful coastal roads in the world. The “technical masterwork” was built in the 1950s and 60s, at the time of Yugoslavian President Tito. Abounding in curves, the asphalt road stretches from Ankaran in Slovenia to Ulcinj in Montenegro. More than half of the road is in Croatia (659 km) and a quarter in Montenegro (125 km). Shorter segments lead through Slovenia; only nine kilometers are in Bosnia and Herzegovina. For all four countries of the former Yugoslavian Federation, the 1,200-kilometer-long highway remains the main thoroughfare of Adriatic tourism. For many travelers, the highway is the absolute dream road. In dizzying heights, it hugs the steep cliffs lining the Adriatic Sea, winds through coves and bays, gardens and stony fields. Wonderful views of the blue sea, green islands, bizarre cliffs and Mediterranean cities and towns are typical of the highway. But with its numerous curves, the dream road also harbors many dangers.

programme.title: mareTV: Madeira - Portugal's sea of blossoms in the Atlantic Ocean
programme.desc: Flower magic in Madeira: The Flower Festival Festa da Flor is the most important event of the year for the people of the Atlantic island. With it they celebrate spring, which is climatically practically all year round here, their island and themselves. The coast formed by lava, centuries-old laurel forests and green steep slopes make Madeira unique. Those who start right at the front of the big parade of the flower festival in the capital Funchal, will have made it. For Isabel Borges this dream has come true. She opens this year's flower parade along the harbour promenade with her festive group. This accolade does not only mean fame and prestige, but also a lot of pressure. Are the self-designed dresses splendid enough? Will the 150 flower children learn the dance steps in time? Will the flowers on the float hold out in the heat? For Isabel, it is now a matter of nerves.

programme.title: mareTV: La Palma: The Greenest of the Canaries
programme.desc: Thundering waterfalls, ancient forests and an impressive volcanic landscape with black beaches: La Palma is a dream island for nature lovers. It is by far the island of the Canary Islands with the most green, almost half of it is covered with forest. But once a year the green island is dominated by the color white. On Rosenmontag (Rose Monday), the inhabitants have for decades been targeting those ancestors who returned from abroad wealthy and ostentatiously demonstrated their wealth with powdered faces. The carnivalistic approach culminates every year in a white chaos, with tons of talcum, flour or paint trickling down the uniformly white dressed islanders. On the Roque de los Muchachos, La Palma's highest mountain at 2,400 meters, stands one of the largest reflecting telescopes in the world. Astrophysicists love the island because it is the perfect place to look into space. Researchers and star lovers look spellbound to Beteigeuze. The giant star is probably in front of a supernova and could become a second moon in the firmament.

programme.title: Giants of Fortune - The Whale Sharks of Oslob
programme.desc: In the little Filipino village of Oslob on the Cebu Island, people suffer from typhoons and overfishing. Until the world’s biggest fish and the Internet change everything.Fisherman Zosimo’s dearest wish is for his children to graduate from high school one day. Yet the chance that this wish will come true is tiny, since at times Zosimo doesn’t even manage to feed the family. Typhoons and overfishing make the lives of Oslob fishermen difficult.

programme.title: The marvellous World of French Rivers
programme.desc: The Gironde is the largest and most powerful tidal current in Europe. When the Gironde flows into the Atlantic, it is 15 kilometers wide and in the rhythm of the tides, it brings the waters from the Pyrenees and the Massif Central into the ocean. This often pushes its waters far out into the Gironde at high tide.This creates a world of its own that has shaped everything uniquely and intensely for tens of thousands of years. The water surface of the river is so large that the evaporation has created its own microclimate, which is stable and, together with the brackish waters, has influenced flora and fauna on the right and left of the bank for a long time.

programme.title: The marvellous World of French Rivers
programme.desc: The Dordogne consists of a visible and an invisible system of flowing water. Caves and basins under the earth's surface store the excess water and return it to the river when it is dry. A perfect management of a precious resource, not invented by humans, but by the complex nature itself. The result is an ever life-giving river.

programme.title: mareTV: Jersey - Sunshine Island in the English Channel
programme.desc: Jersey: the Channel Island is one of the areas in the UK that can boast the most hours of annual sunshine. Not that Dave Cowburn cares very much. He works in the dark, cool ducts of an old bunker from the Sec-ond World War. Here, he breeds turbot, and is very successful at it, too. The "Jersey Royal", the regal potato, has been grown on the island since 1880, fertilized with seaweed from the surrounding ocean. In the third generation, Christine Hellio manages approximately 20 hectares on the coast. "The potato is our most important export commodity", she says. It is harvested by hand, as machines cannot be used on the steep fields. The price is quite regal, too: One kilogram costs 6 Euros. Hugh Gill is one of around 240 voluntary police officers on Jersey. The Honorary Police is regarded as the oldest organised police system in the world. Hugh works for them for one week every month. On the green lanes, the streets of Jersey, the speed limit is 15 miles per hour. Jersey has an immense tidal range and with up to 13 metres difference, it is the world's third largest. This is good for a rarity: the Ormer - one of the world's most expensive species of snail.

programme.title: The Provence coast - Marseille and the Côte Bleue
programme.desc: The Provence is famed for its endless fields of laven-der, but this lush landscape also has a beautifully mari-time touch: The Côte Bleue! Small, hidden beaches, charming harbour towns, imposing, craggy bays and a uniquely clear light that has attracted painters includ-ing Cézanne and Braque. The coast derives its name from the deep blue water and extends from Marseille to Martigues. This small town is also known as "The Ven-ice of the North", as it is shaped entirely by water: an inland lake, the sea itself, as well as a connecting canal. In the bays of the Calanques, the steeply-walled coastal inlets in the Mediterranean limestone, Lionel Franc is a cliff diver. His personal record is a hight of 36 metres! Ambi is a sculptress. This young artist's work, who moved to Marseille from Madagascar many years ago, is characterised by a dynamic momentum. As a pas-sionate pétanque player, she demonstrates this drive on the boules courts of the port city. John Pendray is Pein-tre officiel de la Marine, an official marine painter. The French state allows just 40 painters to its circle. There are no monetary rewards, but heaps of honour and a very smart uniform!

programme.title: Eyes Of The Atacama
programme.desc: ALMA – the Atacama Large Millimeter Array – is the ultimate space observation facility. Here, 66 leviathan parabolic antennae trap cosmic rays in the previously unobservable long-wave range. It can only happen in Atacama, far away from civilisation’s pollution of the night sky with artificial light.

programme.title: Tren Atlantico
programme.desc: We travel by train from the westernmost point of mainland Europe up to Portugal's only national park, the Peneda-Gerês, and from lively Porto to the Spanish border in the northeast. The train takes you from the blue sea to the green Douro Valley, from the urban metropolis to the scorching heat of the deserted hinterland.

programme.title: Tren Atlantico
programme.desc: Switzerland or Spain? This question is often asked by those who see pictures from northern Spain for the first time: High mountains, lonely villages, but - this is the crucial difference - also breathtaking Atlantic beaches. The "Costa Verde", the green coast, is a piece of Spain that is so different from the general tourist image of the Germans' favorite vacation destination. This area has been spared from mass tourism. We travel by train from Bilbao in the Basque Country to Santander in Cantabria and Asturias.

programme.title: Germany's Wild Amazon
programme.desc: As one of Germany’s beauties, the river was the gem of Germanys landscape. But with industrialization it became the country’s hardest working river and like everything that has been overworked, it lost it magnificence and charm. Due to tender love and care, the river is now a reigning example of one of the most successful and outstanding renaturation projects in the country.The film shows never before seen shots of the river now pulsing with life. We will show you the winding river bed, spawning salmon, mating crabs and still-growing anchor ice. You will see dipper birds searching for food under water, kingfishers catching fish, a family life of badgers, foxes and a wide variety of birds. Come and meet the resurrected river Wupper!

programme.title: Germany's Wild Reservoirs
programme.desc: One of the smallest dams in the Bergisches Land is the Panzertalsperre, with an area of just four-and-a-half football pitches. On the other hand, the Dhünntalsperre is the largest with the area of 660 football pitches. They all transform a stretch of flowing water into still and stagnant water. As a result, completely diverse ecosystems have developed there: where the dipper once dived for insect larvae, cormorants and gray herons now fish and swans and coots cavort. In recent summers, even greater challenges have emerged: the effects of climate change - from extreme drought to destructive floods. On a smaller scale, a rather industrious dam master is operating flood protection: The Beaver. However, the water masses of the Wupper tore away half of his majestic timber castle - and the four young beaver kids were not seen again afterwards. Have they survived the flood? Not everyone can cope with the constant change in the dams, but they still remain an important wonder of engineering for many: for us humans as well as for a number of animals. By combining water management, ecological requirements and tourism a worthwhile goal is possible: Because for the Bergisches Land, its dams are among the most valuable and popular infrastructures that the region has to offer.

programme.desc: On July 23rd, 2012, a massive eruption on the sun hurls a colossal cloud of solar matter into space. It’s the most severe sunstorm in 150 years. The coast formed by lava, centuries-old laurel forests and green steep slopes make Madeira unique. Those who start right at the front of the big parade of the flower festival in the capital Funchal, will have made it. For Isabel Borges this dream has come true. She opens this year's flower parade along the harbour promenade with her festive group. This accolade does not only mean fame and prestige, but also a lot of pressure. Are the self-designed dresses splendid enough? Will the 150 flower children learn the dance steps in time? Will the flowers on the float hold out in the heat? For Isabel, it is now a matter of nerves.

programme.title: mareTV: La Palma: The Greenest of the Canaries
programme.desc: Thundering waterfalls, ancient forests and an impressive volcanic landscape with black beaches: La Palma is a dream island for nature lovers. It is by far the island of the Canary Islands with the most green, almost half of it is covered with forest. But once a year the green island is dominated by the color white. On Rosenmontag (Rose Monday), the inhabitants have for decades been targeting those ancestors who returned from abroad wealthy and ostentatiously demonstrated their wealth with powdered faces. The carnivalistic approach culminates every year in a white chaos, with tons of talcum, flour or paint trickling down the uniformly white dressed islanders. On the Roque de los Muchachos, La Palma's highest mountain at 2,400 meters, stands one of the largest reflecting telescopes in the world. Astrophysicists love the island because it is the perfect place to look into space. Researchers and star lovers look spellbound to Beteigeuze. The giant star is probably in front of a supernova and could become a second moon in the firmament.

programme.title: Giants of Fortune - The Whale Sharks of Oslob
programme.desc: In the little Filipino village of Oslob on the Cebu Island, people suffer from typhoons and overfishing. Until the world’s biggest fish and the Internet change everything.Fisherman Zosimo’s dearest wish is for his children to graduate from high school one day. Yet the chance that this wish will come true is tiny, since at times Zosimo doesn’t even manage to feed the family. Typhoons and overfishing make the lives of Oslob fishermen difficult.

programme.title: The marvellous World of French Rivers
programme.desc: The Gironde is the largest and most powerful tidal current in Europe. When the Gironde flows into the Atlantic, it is 15 kilometers wide and in the rhythm of the tides, it brings the waters from the Pyrenees and the Massif Central into the ocean. This often pushes its waters far out into the Gironde at high tide.This creates a world of its own that has shaped everything uniquely and intensely for tens of thousands of years. The water surface of the river is so large that the evaporation has created its own microclimate, which is stable and, together with the brackish waters, has influenced flora and fauna on the right and left of the bank for a long time.

programme.title: The marvellous World of French Rivers
programme.desc: The Dordogne consists of a visible and an invisible system of flowing water. Caves and basins under the earth's surface store the excess water and return it to the river when it is dry. A perfect management of a precious resource, not invented by humans, but by the complex nature itself. The result is an ever life-giving river.

programme.title: mareTV: Jersey - Sunshine Island in the English Channel
programme.desc: Jersey: the Channel Island is one of the areas in the UK that can boast the most hours of annual sunshine. Not that Dave Cowburn cares very much. He works in the dark, cool ducts of an old bunker from the Sec-ond World War. Here, he breeds turbot, and is very successful at it, too. The "Jersey Royal", the regal potato, has been grown on the island since 1880, fertilized with seaweed from the surrounding ocean. In the third generation, Christine Hellio manages approximately 20 hectares on the coast. "The potato is our most important export commodity", she says. It is harvested by hand, as machines cannot be used on the steep fields. The price is quite regal, too: One kilogram costs 6 Euros. Hugh Gill is one of around 240 voluntary police officers on Jersey. The Honorary Police is regarded as the oldest organised police system in the world. Hugh works for them for one week every month. On the green lanes, the streets of Jersey, the speed limit is 15 miles per hour. Jersey has an immense tidal range and with up to 13 metres difference, it is the world's third largest. This is good for a rarity: the Ormer - one of the world's most expensive species of snail.

programme.title: The Provence coast - Marseille and the Côte Bleue
programme.desc: The Provence is famed for its endless fields of laven-der, but this lush landscape also has a beautifully mari-time touch: The Côte Bleue! Small, hidden beaches, charming harbour towns, imposing, craggy bays and a uniquely clear light that has attracted painters includ-ing Cézanne and Braque. The coast derives its name from the deep blue water and extends from Marseille to Martigues. This small town is also known as "The Ven-ice of the North", as it is shaped entirely by water: an inland lake, the sea itself, as well as a connecting canal. In the bays of the Calanques, the steeply-walled coastal inlets in the Mediterranean limestone, Lionel Franc is a cliff diver. His personal record is a hight of 36 metres! Ambi is a sculptress. This young artist's work, who moved to Marseille from Madagascar many years ago, is characterised by a dynamic momentum. As a pas-sionate pétanque player, she demonstrates this drive on the boules courts of the port city. John Pendray is Pein-tre officiel de la Marine, an official marine painter. The French state allows just 40 painters to its circle. There are no monetary rewards, but heaps of honour and a very smart uniform!

programme.title: Eyes Of The Atacama
programme.desc: ALMA – the Atacama Large Millimeter Array – is the ultimate space observation facility. Here, 66 leviathan parabolic antennae trap cosmic rays in the previously unobservable long-wave range. It can only happen in Atacama, far away from civilisation’s pollution of the night sky with artificial light.

programme.title: Tren Atlantico
programme.desc: We travel by train from the westernmost point of mainland Europe up to Portugal's only national park, the Peneda-Gerês, and from lively Porto to the Spanish border in the northeast. The train takes you from the blue sea to the green Douro Valley, from the urban metropolis to the scorching heat of the deserted hinterland.

programme.title: Tren Atlantico
programme.desc: Switzerland or Spain? This question is often asked by those who see pictures from northern Spain for the first time: High mountains, lonely villages, but - this is the crucial difference - also breathtaking Atlantic beaches. The "Costa Verde", the green coast, is a piece of Spain that is so different from the general tourist image of the Germans' favorite vacation destination. This area has been spared from mass tourism. We travel by train from Bilbao in the Basque Country to Santander in Cantabria and Asturias.

programme.title: Germany's Wild Amazon
programme.desc: As one of Germany’s beauties, the river was the gem of Germanys landscape. But with industrialization it became the country’s hardest working river and like everything that has been overworked, it lost it magnificence and charm. Due to tender love and care, the river is now a reigning example of one of the most successful and outstanding renaturation projects in the country.The film shows never before seen shots of the river now pulsing with life. We will show you the winding river bed, spawning salmon, mating crabs and still-growing anchor ice. You will see dipper birds searching for food under water, kingfishers catching fish, a family life of badgers, foxes and a wide variety of birds. Come and meet the resurrected river Wupper!

programme.title: Germany's Wild Reservoirs
programme.desc: One of the smallest dams in the Bergisches Land is the Panzertalsperre, with an area of just four-and-a-half football pitches. On the other hand, the Dhünntalsperre is the largest with the area of 660 football pitches. They all transform a stretch of flowing water into still and stagnant water. As a result, completely diverse ecosystems have developed there: where the dipper once dived for insect larvae, cormorants and gray herons now fish and swans and coots cavort. In recent summers, even greater challenges have emerged: the effects of climate change - from extreme drought to destructive floods. On a smaller scale, a rather industrious dam master is operating flood protection: The Beaver. However, the water masses of the Wupper tore away half of his majestic timber castle - and the four young beaver kids were not seen again afterwards. Have they survived the flood? Not everyone can cope with the constant change in the dams, but they still remain an important wonder of engineering for many: for us humans as well as for a number of animals. By combining water management, ecological requirements and tourism a worthwhile goal is possible: Because for the Bergisches Land, its dams are among the most valuable and popular infrastructures that the region has to offer.

programme.title: The Sun - Inferno in the Sky
programme.desc: On July 23rd, 2012, a massive eruption on the sun hurls a colossal cloud of solar matter into space. It’s the most severe sunstorm in 150 years. Fortunately, the Earth is not in the direct path of this solar ejection. But it’s only a matter of time before a violent solar storm hits us. When these clouds of charged matter reach our planet, they can wreak havoc in electrical systems.

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Roads are more than just gray strips of asphalt that allow us to travel and trade. For centuries they have been lifelines of mankind, full of stories and history - and in certain countries and areas they also hold great dangers, much human suffering and death. Documentary filmmaker Oliver G. Becker ventured onto the dangerous roads of Afghanistan's Hindu Kush Mountains, the infamous Moloto Road in South Africa, along the vertiginous slopes of the Bolivian Andes and other "roads of death" in India, Georgia and the Ivory Coast

programme.title: Deadly Roads
programme.desc: Some risks on these autoroutes have natural causes: Extreme weather, avalanches and landslides. In some areas, the locals even believe that evil spirits kill travelers. But many of the dangers are man-made: robbers or terrorists lie in wait for travelers, and tough labor pressures, social hardship and greedy mass-transit businesses also cause tragic driving accidents around the world. In the 20th century alone, 35 million people died on roads worldwide - plus 1.5 billion injured! With the two-part "Death Roads - On the Road at the Limit," phoenix offers a documentary road movie along the world's most dangerous car routes.

programme.title: Menorca - Majorca's beautiful sister
programme.desc: Not nearly as crowded as Majorca or Ibiza: Menorca has noticeably fewer visitors than her sister islands and in 1993, was recognised by UNESCO as a biosphere re-serve. Menorca also has its own distinctive charm, with its secluded coves, mighty cliffs, beautiful gardens and ages old towns and villages. Its residents love the is-lands treasures and peculiarities. Forests make up al-most a third of Menorca, complemented by many lush green meadows. Next to tourism, agriculture is a major source of the island's income to the present day. On Menorca, there are several accumulations of enormous megalithic stones. From a global point of view, the up to five-metre-tall "Taulas", whereby the stones are ar-ranged in the shape of a "T", are unique.

programme.title: Wild Sardinia
programme.desc: Sardinia has always been the epitome of pure wilderness, an emerald of volcanic origin in the Mediterranean. 1900 metres of coastline and an infinite maze of offshore islands. But Sardinia also has other facets: green valleys, rugged mountains, murmuring brooks, mysterious ruins and a unique fauna. Just off of Sardinia's coast is an untouched underwater paradise - uniquely beautiful, but also dangerous. Pilot whales, dolphins and mobula rays populate the waters at Capo Testa in the north of the island. In the west, the lagoons of Cabras represent a wild landscape of lakes in which thousands of flamingos live and hunt the red brine shrimps. In addition to the flamingos, grey and purple herons and little egrets breed here. Thousands of bats have found refuge in the craggy mountain world of the Supramonte and Gennargentu, with their countless grottoes and caves. In the sea we can observe the mass mating of sea slugs, and thanks to our camera robots and submersible boats we were able to observe beard worms with luminous red gills, as well as bright yellow tree corals in the area surrounding the hypothermal lava holes.

programme.title: Dead Bride
programme.desc: Als Alyson (Jennifer Mischiati) und Richard (Christoph Hülsen) ein neues Haus beziehen, das ihnen Alysons leiblicher Vater hinterlassen hat, wissen sie noch nicht, welcher Horror ihnen bevorsteht. Ein dunkles Geheimnis lauert zwischen den Wänden und wartet darauf, die Neuankömmlinge zu verschlingen.

programme.title: Against the Night - Nur einer überlebt!
programme.desc: Das gegenseitige Vertrauen einer Gruppe von Freunden wird auf die blutige Probe gestellt, als sie zusammen in ein altes, verlassenes Gefängnis einbrechen. Nachdem der Erste von ihnen plötzlich vermisst wird, verdächtigen sie sich gegenseitig, etwas mit dem Verschwinden des Freundes zu tun zu haben. Bis sie bemerken, dass sie vielleicht nicht allein im Inneren der Ruine sind …

programme.title: Eradication - Contact Kills
programme.desc: Verwüstet durch eine Pandemie, ist die Gesellschaft zusammengebrochen. David Baldwin, ein asymptomatischer Träger der Krankheit, wird zu Studienzwecken in Isolation gehalten. Sein einziger Kontakt ist per Video zu seiner Frau Sam, einer Epidemiologin, die sein Blut erforscht, um Heilung zu finden. Aber David beginnt zu glauben, dass man ihm nicht die Wahrheit sagt und Sam in Gefahr sein könnte.

programme.title: Alien Conspiracies - Sind sie unter uns?
programme.desc: Bestimmen Außerirdische die Vergangenheit, Gegenwart und Zukunft der Menschheit? Seit Anbeginn der Zeit beschäftigt die Menschheit die Frage „Weshalb sind wir hier?“. Vom Mysterium antiker Alien-Gestalten bis hin zu modernen Verschwörungstheorien im Internet - für einige Forscher ist der Einfluss von Außerirdischen auf die Welt, wie wir sie kennen, unbestritten

programme.title: Madame Annie und ihre Familie
programme.desc: Als Annie (Alexandra Lamy) einen positiven Schwangerschaftstest im Badezimmer entdeckt, beginnen turbulente Zeiten für die Großfamilie Castillon. Gehört der Test der Freundin ihres älteren Sohnes oder der Teenager-Tochter? Wird Annie - welch‘ schrecklicher Gedanke - jetzt schon Großmutter? Oder hat ihr Mann Laurent eine Geliebte?

programme.title: Rosie & Frank - Wiedersehen auf vier Pfoten
programme.desc: Vor zwei Jahren verlor Róise ihren geliebten Frank, doch ein mysteriöser Hund bringt plötzlich Freude zurück in ihr Leben. Róise ist überzeugt, dass Frank in diesem besonderen Vierbeiner wiedergeboren wurde, als er sich so leidenschaftlich fürs Dorfleben interessiert. Zwischen Lachen und Tränen entfaltet sich eine bewegende Geschichte über die heilende Kraft der Liebe und magische Neuanfänge.

programme.title: Kartoffelsalat 3 - Das Musical
programme.desc: Wegen zu wenig Schulnachwuchs auf dem Land soll eine Lehranstalt schließen. So muss die geliebte Schule um Direktor Leo Weiß mit dem spießigen Elitegymnasium, konkurrieren. Die Anzahl der Neuanmeldungen soll entscheiden. Um die Beliebtheit der Schule zu steigern, kommt die engagierte Schülersprecherin Mia auf eine Idee: ein selbst inszeniertes Musical über die damalige Zombie-Epidemie!

programme.title: Kartoffelsalat - Nicht fragen
programme.desc: Leo Weiß hat ein schweres Leben an seiner Schule. Er ist der Klassenälteste, kämpft mit schlechten Noten und mangelnder Anerkennung. So beschließen seine Eltern ihn auf eine neue Schule zu schicken, in der Hoffnung auf einen Neuanfang. Als ein bedrohlicher Virus ausbricht, der aus Schülern fresssüchtige Infizierte macht, ergreift Leo die Initiative und beweist sich als Held.

programme.title: Der Sportpenner
programme.desc: Charlie Meinhart strandet auf einer Parkbank in Berlin, doch sein Durst nach Glück führt ihn nach Biarritz. Im sonnigen Südwesten Frankreichs, wo Sport und Meer verschmelzen, entdeckt er eine neue Leidenschaft: Sport. Gemeinsam mit anderen Obdachlosen wird er zum Sportfreak. Doch ob sein neues Lebensmotto ohne Geld und Zuhause, dafür mit Sport und einem Glas Wein, ihn tatsächlich ins Glück führt?

programme.title: Die Kleinen und die Bösen
programme.desc: In einer rabenschwarzen Komödie trifft ein deutscher Bewährungshelfer auf eine verrückte Truppe, die seine Nerven strapazieren. Skurrile Charaktere und absurde Zwischenfälle sorgen für ein Chaos, das zwischen Gesetz und Anarchie balanciert. Dabei entpuppt sich mancher als weniger böse als gedacht.

programme.title: Fixed - Kleiner Schnitt, große Panik
programme.desc: Allan ist glücklich verheiratet und dreifacher, stolzer Vater. Als seine Frau sich jedoch weigert, weiterhin die Pille zu nehmen, verpasst das seinem Sexleben einen heftigen Schlag. Schnell sieht Allan sich mit einem Termin zur Sterilisation und einer Midlife-Crisis konfrontiert. Denn obwohl er ein treuer Gatte ist, treibt ihn der Gedanke an den ärztlichen Eingriff in den Wahnsinn.

programme.title: Chasers - Zu sexy für den Knast
programme.desc: Die beiden Militärpolizisten Rock (Tom Berenger) und Eddie (William McNamara) sollen eine gutaussehende Blondine (Erika Eleniak) ins Militärgefängnis überführen. Das Problem dabei ist, dass die Dame keinesfalls vorhat, die Strafe anzutreten und mit allen erdenklichen Tricks versucht, ihren Bewachern zu entkommen …

programme.title: Fette Kumpelz
programme.desc: Bob und Rashid geraten wegen ihres 'Kiffer-Lebensstils' in Schwierigkeiten mit der Polizei. Ein alter Freund entpuppt sich als verdeckter Ermittler...

programme.title: MORGAN: Killer Doll
programme.desc: Darcy, Astrids geheimnisvolle Freundin aus der Kindheit, kehrt nach vielen Jahren zurück und bringt eine unheimliche Puppe mit, die ihr bis aufs Haar gleicht. Als Darcy von Astrids Clique verspottet wird, setzt ihr schockierender Selbstmord eine grausige Kette von Ereignissen in Gang. Nach und nach verschwinden Astrids Freunde, während die Puppe auf unerklärliche Weise zum Leben erwacht.

programme.title: Jack in the Box - ES lebt
programme.desc: Nachdem ein alter Schachtelteufel geöffnet und in den Besitz eines Museums übergeben wurde, befällt den Angestellten Casey Reynolds schnell der Verdacht, dass die gruselige Clown-Puppe ein Eigenleben führt. Als seine Kollegen einer nach dem anderen sterben, sucht Casey verzweifelt einen Weg, um diesen tödlichen Albtraum zu stoppen …

programme.title: Dämon - Dunkle Vergangenheit
programme.desc: Geplagt von unaussprechlichen Geistern kämpft eine Familie gegen finstere Mächte, die ihr Glück bedrohen. Vera, Ray und Sam sind gefangen in einem Netz aus Schrecken und Geheimnissen. Während die Eltern alles versuchen, um ihren Sohn vor der düsteren Wahrheit zu bewahren, entfaltet sich ein Horror, der die Familie in einen gnadenlosen Kampf gegen Dämonen führt.
